_what: Where each model call Trillion makes for a person goes, in order (src/model-routes.mjs, used by the person store's askThroughRoutes for src/model-calls.mjs and by src/attention.mjs). A `device` route asks a model on the person's own computer through a Workshop tool that runs there (tool_id, on placement:your-computer; computer/local-models.json says which local servers answer), free to them and to Trillion; a computer that is asleep or has no such model answers nothing and the next route is tried. A `picked` route asks the services the person picked for their own AIs' work (order_your_ais), each send counted and refused before it leaves once the person's spend budget for that account is reached (src/api-spend.mjs, src/spend-meter.json; the starting budget is $0 a day, so a key billed by the word is never asked until they set one). Resumable work is handed to the person's connected subscription AIs first. The your-ais admission rule identifies that work; other conversation work tries the device and picked routes as before. Each explicit job route order is honored, and an unjudged synchronous check never becomes queued background work. Why it exists: on 2026-10-05 every conversation went to the person's Gemini key with no limit and cost them $103 in a few hours. `conversation` are the routes a conversation (messages) tries; `classify` the routes a yes-or-no question about some words tries (src/attention.mjs). A device route's `wait_seconds` is how long the asker waits for the answer, and `take_within_seconds` how long the ask may wait in the computer's queue before it is let go unanswered: a computer that has not taken it by then is busy with newer asks, and answering it later would only answer someone who has already gone (2026-10-07: with 50 asks queued oldest first, the Mac took judge asks after 90 s on average, as their askers stopped waiting, and every step waited out its asks one by one). A new route is a row here. `calling` holds the routes of the AI calling Trillion through MCP, listed apart from `conversation` so a job without its own routes walks the same order as before (a job names one in its `routes`). A job's `hedge` ({ after_seconds, most_input_chars }) asks the picked services beside the computer when it has not answered after after_seconds, and the first good answer wins (src/model-routes.mjs hedgedRoads); an answer that arrives second is dropped. A job whose input is longer than most_input_chars is never asked twice. The picked route is still refused before it leaves once the person's spend budget is reached, so at the starting $0 budget nothing is paid.

conversation._what: When reached in the declared route order, work of a purpose this rule admits is kept immediately as an ask for the AIs the person already pays for (src/asks-for-your-ais.mjs): one job handed to them asks them to answer what waits with the MCP tools model_asks_waiting and answer_model_ask, and the work finds the answer by the ask's identity when it runs again. Only work that runs again by itself belongs here (the reading of what came in, stories, privacy rewrites, outcome checks, the weighing of what the places a person follows brought, src/watch-sources.mjs; linking grounded files to recorded pursuits; the daily website article, whose job sends the same ask again until it is answered, worker/model-road.js of trillion-site); a check judged inside a decision step is answered there or taken unjudged, so it never waits. Why it exists: on 2026-10-07 an account's hourly reading (60,000 characters) had failed since 2026-10-05 because the model on the person's own computer could not fit it in 45 seconds and their key was held at a $0 budget.
conversation.job: Answer what Trillion needs your AIs to read for this person: call model_asks_waiting, answer each ask by following its messages exactly as the model they were written for (when they ask for JSON, reply with the JSON alone), and send each reply with answer_model_ask. These are resumable tasks for any connected AI on this person's account. A local model or metered API key is not a prerequisite. Respect each ask's source and requested format, and keep private input within this account. Finish when none waits.
conversation.said: Answer what Trillion needs your AIs to read for you

calling._what: The AI calling Trillion through MCP judges the checks itself, on the subscription the person already pays for (Claude, ChatGPT, Codex): method_questions hands each check to it, with the words of the active grader, and decide_in_one_pass takes its verdicts beside each answer and checks them (src/check-judge.mjs takeCallerVerdicts). A verdict must name what it rests on (a quote of the answer or an evidence ref of the case) and who gave it (graded_by), for every grader. `grader` picks who judges, and it is data: "self" (the calling AI judges its own checks), "second-judge" (the calling AI hands the checks to a second, independent judge with fresh context, a different model where the host offers one, on the same subscription, and sends those verdicts), "cross-ai" (another of the person's connected AIs would judge through the hand-off queue; no hand-off path is built yet, so it is accepted and its words ask for a second judge, as "second-judge" does). Trillion and the person's API keys pay nothing for these verdicts, and they are never kept in judge memory. Why "second-judge" (measured 2026-10-09 on 92 real check answers with known verdicts, fleet judge-eval): every grader on the person's subscription agreed with the known verdicts more often than the per-token claude-haiku-4-5 route this replaced (80.4%, with good answers refused) and matched or beat the model on their own computer at about a ninth of the time (about 47 s against 424-431 s a set); a second Sonnet judge whose every verdict quoted the words it rests on reached 93.5% (code checks only that the quote is words of the answer, eight characters or more, or an evidence ref, and that a refusal names the check's own words; it does not judge whether the quote supports the verdict); self against second judge on the same model differed by 1-2 items either way, within noise, so second-judge is kept because it was never measurably worse and published work finds judges favour answers they wrote themselves (Panickssery et al. 2024; Huang et al. 2023); another connected AI (Codex) judged as well as a second judge but about seven times slower. This route asks no model itself: askThroughRoutes (src/person-store.mjs) skips it, and what it answers arrives with the request.

grader_words.self: Judge each check of this answer yourself, honestly. Send your verdicts beside this answer in answers as verdicts: [{ check, meets, rests_on, missing?, graded_by }]. check is the id of a checklist item above; meets says whether the answer meets that check; rests_on quotes words of this answer (at least eight characters) or names an evidence ref of the case that the verdict rests on; missing, only when meets is false, copies exactly the words of the check the answer does not address; graded_by names you, the model or agent that judged. A verdict that does not meet these rules is ignored, and its check is judged as usual.
grader_words.second-judge: Hand each check of this answer to a second judge with fresh context: a subagent, or a different model where your host offers one, on the same subscription. Give it the check, this answer and the evidence of the case, and nothing of how the answer was drafted. Send its verdicts beside this answer in answers as verdicts: [{ check, meets, rests_on, missing?, graded_by }]. check is the id of a checklist item above; meets says whether the answer meets that check; rests_on quotes words of this answer (at least eight characters) or names an evidence ref of the case; missing, only when meets is false, copies exactly the words of the check the answer does not address; graded_by names that second judge (its model or agent name). A verdict that does not meet these rules is ignored, and its check is judged as usual.
grader_words.cross-ai: Another of your connected AIs cannot be handed these checks yet, so hand each check of this answer to a second judge with fresh context: a subagent, or a different model where your host offers one, on the same subscription. Give it the check, this answer and the evidence of the case, and nothing of how the answer was drafted. Send its verdicts beside this answer in answers as verdicts: [{ check, meets, rests_on, missing?, graded_by }]. check is the id of a checklist item above; meets says whether the answer meets that check; rests_on quotes words of this answer (at least eight characters) or names an evidence ref of the case; missing, only when meets is false, copies exactly the words of the check the answer does not address; graded_by names that second judge (its model or agent name). A verdict that does not meet these rules is ignored, and its check is judged as usual.

check-judge._what: The check judge answers one yes-or-no verdict per check. The AI calling Trillion judges the checks it was handed itself first, at no cost (calling-ai: decide_in_one_pass takes its verdicts), and only the checks it left are asked of the person's computer. The person's picked service is a route of this job only when the person opted in for it (opt_in_routes, listed in the person's model_opt_ins fact): then it is asked after the calling AI, on the cheapest model that service sells (each has a price row in src/api-spend.json, so the spend budget counts it), before the computer. Without an opt-in nothing is sent to a key, and a check nothing answers is taken unjudged. 2026-10-08 a decision of 15 steps took minutes because every verdict waited in the Mac's queue.

outcome-judge._what: `role` (and optionally `effort`) names the loadout the device route asks for this job (loadouts below, src/model-routes.mjs modelsFor): the job asks those models in that order instead of its models in records/local-model-records.json.

loadouts._what: Model choice as role loadouts: a profile maps each role (general, cheap, structured, and any role a row adds) to the models to try in order, primary first and fallbacks after, as ids of records/local-model-records.json (local-model-server rows). The person's effort picks the profile, not a model name: `efforts` maps an effort to a profile id and `default_effort` is used when none is given. `credit_ceilings` is the most credits one request of a profile should cost, carried to the asker as a hint (`credit_ceiling` from modelsFor; null when a profile names none): nothing here enforces spending, and every shipped profile asks only models on the person's own computer, so 0. A job names its loadout with `role` (and `effort`) in `jobs`. A new role, profile or effort is a row here (src/model-routes.mjs modelsFor).

waiting._what: Work that needed a model and found none answering (a story, a privacy rewrite, an outcome check) waits and runs again by itself (src/model-waits.mjs): first after first_seconds, each later try twice as far out up to longest_seconds, never dropped; batch is how many run at one alarm, one after another.
waiting.said: No model of yours answered just now, so this waits and is done by itself when one does.
